3_viaductes.full_name: The Three Viaducts (Lower, Middle and High)
3_viaductes.description: A series of pathways and viaducts built on tilted stone columns rusticly integrated into the natural hillside landscape.

casa_museu.description: Antoni Gaudí's personal residence for nearly 20 years (1906-1925), originally designed by Francesc Berenguer.

escalinata_drac.description: Monumental entrance staircase featuring the famous multicolored mosaic (trencadís) salamander/dragon.

pavellons_consergeria.description: Entrance pavilions with undulating mosaic rooftops inspired by the fairy tale Hansel and Gretel.

placa_natura.description: Large open esplanade bordered by the famous serpentine mosaic bench designed with Josep Maria Jujol.

sala_hipostila.description: Covered hall with 86 Doric-inspired columns originally intended as the residential estate's marketplace.

turo_3_creus.description: Highest point of the park with a stone monument topped by three crosses, offering panoramic views over Barcelona.

cupula.description: Towering cupolas and hyperbolic vaults enclosing the central naves and apse of the basilica.

facana_naixement.description: The only façade constructed almost entirely during Gaudí's lifetime, renowned for its intricate, naturalistic ornamentation celebrating the birth of Jesus.

facana_passio.description: Austere and dramatic façade depicting the suffering and death of Christ, featuring angular sculptures by Josep Maria Subirachs.

laterals.description: Exterior structures, walls, and stained-glass window portals of the side aisles adorned with geometric and botanical motifs.

posterior.description: The posterior apse section surrounding the crypt, decorated with gargoyles depicting reptiles and amphibians.

torres.description: Conical bell towers topped with colorful mosaic pinnacles dedicated to the apostles and evangelists.
